newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index dips 0.4 pts on losses to Nafta.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index dips 0.4 pts on losses to Nafta.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Thursday, with the SAX index dipping 0.4 points to 188.98 on losses to shares of oil and gas storage company Nafta.
Nafta fell 100 crowns to 1,850 from 1,950 on Wednesday, though dealers said its current price appears more in line with its true value.
Jozef Cimra of ING Barings, however, pointed out that small volumes traded with Nafta stocks, some 645 shares on Thursday, which made it difficult to predict the issue's future development.

The most-capitalised issue on the bourse, oil refiner Slovnaft, lost one crown to close at 800, with brokers saying the current price also reflected its real market value and that they were optimistic over its possible development in near future.

"From the point of view of foreign investors, there now seems to be favourable conditions for investing in Slovnaft," Cimra said. "The price is relatively low which, together with the company's fundamentals and its ambitious modernisation plans, can be a good reason for investing in it," he added.

Overall vollume fell to 665,424 shares, of which direct trades accounted for the major part, from 786,557 stocks traded on Wednesday. The turnover decreased to 361.90 million crowns from 389.78 million on Wednesday.
